A new poll from The Economist/YouGov shows Democrats have an 8-point lead on a generic House ballot. The polling also found that President Trump's approval rating dropped to 33%. MS NOW Senior Editor and Opinion Columnist Anthony Fisher, Democratic strategist Basil Smikle, independent journalist Ahmed Baba and CNBC Fast Money Contributor Dan Nathan join Antonia Hylton to share their analysis as the midterms inch closer.

results.title: New Poll: Dems have 8-point lead on generic House ballot, Trump approval sinks to 33%

results.content:
Democrats currently lead registered voters 46% to 39% in the Economist/YouGov generic congressional ballot. Among voters who say they are extremely enthusiastic about voting, the gap is much wider: 60% say they plan to vote Democratic, compared with 37% Republican.

Trump’s MAGA base remains intact. The question facing Republicans is whether the broader coalition that returned him to power still exists. For now, the numbers suggest it is beginning to fracture. [...] An Economist/YouGov poll painted a similarly difficult picture. Fifty-seven percent said going to war was the wrong decision, while only 25% said it was the right one. results.content: Recent polling data, however, suggests challenges for the GOP. A national Economist/YouGov poll released on August 4 shows Democrats leading Republicans by 8 points on the generic ballot. Additionally, Trump's approval rating has fallen to 36%, with 60% disapproving of his performance as president.
